refuted_claims.lens: THE END-USER JOURNEY — DOES IT ACTUALLY WORK? (5 personas simulated against a fresh clone)
refuted_claims.title: README claims `.claude/commands/` ships in-tree; .gitignore excludes it, so a fresh clone has zero slash commands
refuted_claims.reason:
Three independently falsifiable assertions in the claim are all false.

(1) The quoted README line does not exist. README.md is 197 lines; line 45 is "With this library loaded, it writes this instead:" (prose introducing an Apex snippet). A repo-wide `grep -rn "ships in-tree" . --exclude-dir=.git` returns ZERO hits — the string does not appear anywhere in the repository. There is no such table, no "Auto" column, no in-tree promise. README's actual Claude Code line (README.md:88) says only "Claude Code picks the repo up automatically via `CLAUDE.md`" — a true statement about CLAUDE.md, making no claim about `.claude/commands/`. The claim invents the very text it refutes.

(2) "grepping README.md, CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/*.md for `install_local_commands` returns zero hits — it is documented only inside its own module docstring." False. That exact grep returns 8 hits across 4 doc files: docs/getting-started.md (4x, including a copy-pasteable quick-start block AND sample output), docs/troubleshooting.md (2x), docs/architecture.md (1x), docs/worked-example-trigger-consolidation.md (1x). Moreover docs/getting-started.md:63-69 documents the .gitignore situation verbatim as a named gotcha — "**2. There are no slash commands.** `.gitignore` contains `.claude/*` (negated only for `.claude/workflows/`), and `git ls-files .claude/commands` returns 0 files. The 65 tracked command specs live in `commands/`. `python3 scripts/install_local_commands.py` is what puts them where Claude Code looks." — then puts that command in the canonical clone recipe at line 83. The exact discovery the claim presents as an unshipped P0 is already the second item in the repo's own getting-started doc.

(3) "`git ls-files .claude/` returns exactly one file … A fresh clone's `.claude/` contains only `workflows/`." False. It returns 72 files: 48 under .claude/agents/, 23 under .claude/skills/, 1 under .claude/workflows/ (already-tracked paths survive a later `.claude/*` ignore). A fresh clone gets agents/, skills/ and workflows/, not workflows/ alone.

What IS true: `.gitignore:81-82` is `.claude/*` + `!.claude/workflows/`, and `git ls-files .claude/commands/` returns 0, so slash commands do require the one-line install step. That is a deliberate, commented design decision (.gitignore:77-80 explains the `/*` + `!` pattern) with a shipped repair script and four docs pages covering it — not an undocumented P0 contradiction. The only residual nit is P3 at most: README's own quick-start (lines 84-91) does not itself mention `install_local_commands.py`, deferring to docs/getting-started.md.
refuted_claims.corrected: Not a P0. No README text claims `.claude/commands/` ships in-tree (the quoted line 45 does not exist anywhere in the repo), and `install_local_commands.py` is documented in 4 doc files with the .gitignore exclusion called out explicitly as a named gotcha in docs/getting-started.md:63-69 plus included in the canonical clone recipe at line 83. The only defensible residual is P3/cosmetic: README.md's own quick-start block (lines 84-91) omits `python3 scripts/install_local_commands.py`, so a reader who never opens docs/getting-started.md gets no slash commands; adding that one line (or a pointer to getting-started) to README would close it.

refuted_claims.lens: THE END-USER JOURNEY — DOES IT ACTUALLY WORK? (5 personas simulated against a fresh clone)
refuted_claims.title: The search tool indexes zero agents, commands, decision trees, or templates — no persona could discover the agent built for their task
refuted_claims.reason: Reproduced the census exactly (130,062 chunks; skills/knowledge/standards/https only), so the raw index fact holds. Everything built on top of it fails. First, the claim's own evidence is wrong: rerunning persona query 1 returns a ranked skill hit, not "Coverage: NONE". Second, the "fresh clone" framing collapses — chunks.jsonl is gitignored, so on a fresh clone `search_knowledge.py` has nothing to search; the router skill itself documents this ("This needs `vector_index/`, which is **not shipped** ... If the command errors or reports `Coverage: NONE`, fall back to mechanism 1"). Third, the assertion "the only task→agent router in the product requires installing and running the MCP server" is directly contradicted by the shipped plugin: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` ships `./.claude/skills/` (12 router skills), the top-level `salesforce` router contains a full run-time agent roster by domain plus the decision-tree list the claim says is unreachable, and 65 slash commands each name their agent. That surface is live in this very session — `/assess-org`, `/plan-bulk-migration`, `/preflight-load` and the `salesforce*` routers all appear in the available-skills list with descriptions, with no MCP server connected. The grep for `suggest_agent` hitting only `mcp/` is true but irrelevant: agent routing in the plugin channel is done by description matching over commands/subagents, not by a function named `suggest_agent`.
refuted_claims.corrected: Narrowly true and low-severity: `vector_index/chunks.jsonl` contains no chunks from `agents/`, `commands/`, `templates/`, or `standards/decision-trees/`, and `search_knowledge.py` exposes only `--domain`/`--json` (no `--agents`). But the P0 conclusion is wrong on three counts. (1) `vector_index/chunks.jsonl` is gitignored (`.gitignore:14`) — a fresh clone has no chunks at all, so the lexical index was never the fresh-clone discovery path; the shipped, zero-setup surfaces are 65 tracked `commands/*.md`, 197 tracked files under `agents/`, and the 23 tracked plugin router skills under `.claude/skills/`. (2) The MCP server is NOT the only task→agent router: `.claude/skills/salesforce/SKILL.md` (generated by `scripts/build_plugin.py`, shipped in the plugin manifest) carries an explicit "## Run-time agents" roster grouped by domain at line 131, plus a decision-tree index and cross-domain entry points — and each of the 65 slash commands names the agent it triggers (`commands/assess-org.md`: "Triggers the **org-assessor** agent"). Command and router-skill descriptions are what an assistant matches a persona's phrasing against; no MCP install required. `scripts/search_skills.py` additionally offers role/cloud-boosted, synonym-expanded skill search. (3) The evidence output is partly misreported: persona query 1 does NOT return "Coverage: NONE" — it returns `admin/org-cleanup-and-technical-debt (1.520)`. A reasonable residual ask is a `--kind agents` flag on the CLI for parity with MCP `suggest_agent`, which is a P3 nice-to-have, not a P0 "no persona could discover the agent".

refuted_claims.lens: THE END-USER JOURNEY — DOES IT ACTUALLY WORK? (5 personas simulated against a fresh clone)
refuted_claims.title: Confidence gating is inverted: a fabricated Salesforce product returns a high-confidence skill with no caveat, while a real covered topic returns "Coverage: NONE"
refuted_claims.reason:
Three of the four load-bearing assertions fail.

(1) THE EVIDENCE DOES NOT REPRODUCE. They report "security/platform-encryption (3.073)" as the sole top skill. The actual run returns TWO skills with completely different scores: architect/hipaa-compliance-architecture (1.331) and security/platform-encryption (0.806). Their "3.073" figure exists nowhere in current output — it is a cumulative-score number from a gate version superseded by the OR-form gate documented in config/retrieval-config.yaml ("swept on 2026-07-31"). The quoted output is stale.

(2) "There is no signal distinguishing 'your query names something I have no skill for' from 'I have a strong match'" is FLATLY FALSE. `has_coverage` is a first-class boolean in the JSON payload (scripts/search_knowledge.py:305), rendered as the literal "Coverage: NONE" banner (line 356-357), and consumed by commands/new-skill.md:21, commands/request-skill.md:41-46, commands/build-skills.md:66, and agents/_shared/SKILL_BUILDER_CORE.md:45-46. It is exactly the signal they say does not exist.

(3) THE SIGNAL DEMONSTRABLY FIRES on out-of-corpus queries. Pure nonsense returns Coverage: NONE:
  "zorblax frobnicator quibblesnort" -> has_coverage False, []
  "xyzzy plugh thudfoo"              -> has_coverage False, []
Their probe returned coverage not because the gate is broken but because "Salesforce Quantum Ledger blockchain OBJECT ENCRYPTION" contains two real, heavily-covered Salesforce terms. Returning Shield Platform Encryption for a query containing "object encryption" is correct retrieval, not a hallucination. Only "Quantum Ledger blockchain" is fabricated; the corpus never claimed that product exists.

(4) THE GATE IS NOT INVERTED. It reads max_score/score, NOT rank_score — and scripts/search_knowledge.py:247-254 carries an explicit comment saying the name/description bonus is deliberately excluded so "a title coincidence [cannot] manufacture coverage the corpus lacks." The design already anticipates the exact failure mode alleged.

WHAT SURVIVES: the second half reproduces. "migrate 5 million records into Salesforce" -> has_coverage False, despite skills/data/bulk-api-and-large-data-loads existing. That is a genuine false-negative. But it is a single-phrasing calibration miss, not a systemic inversion — every near-paraphrase passes:
  "bulk api data load"                     -> True  [data/bulk-api-and-large-data-loads]
  "load millions of records with Bulk API" -> True  [data/bulk-api-patterns]
  "data migration planning"                -> True  [data/data-migration-planning]
  "large data volume migration strategy"   -> True
The config documents this residual explicitly and quantifies it: fixture false-NONE 0, held-out NONE 6.7% (down from 23.3% pre-sweep). A known, measured, already-reduced tail — not a P0 broken safety mechanism.
refuted_claims.corrected: Not a P0 and not an inversion. The confidence gate (`has_coverage`) exists, is documented, is consumed by four downstream commands/agents, and correctly returns "Coverage: NONE" for genuinely out-of-corpus queries (verified with pure-nonsense probes). The real, much smaller issue: the gate produces occasional false negatives on natural-language phrasings of covered topics — "migrate 5 million records into Salesforce" returns Coverage: NONE even though data/bulk-api-and-large-data-loads covers it, while four near-paraphrases of the same intent all pass. This is the known ~6.7% held-out false-NONE tail already measured and documented in config/retrieval-config.yaml (reduced from 23.3% by the 2026-07-31 OR-gate sweep), and is a P3 retrieval-tuning item — candidate fix is a trigger-phrase addition to the bulk-load skill for numeric-scale phrasings ("5 million records", "migrate N million"). The "fabricated product returns high confidence" half should be dropped entirely: the probe query contained the real, well-covered terms "object encryption", so the encryption skill match was correct behavior, and the quoted score of 3.073 does not reproduce against current code.

refuted_claims.lens: THE END-USER JOURNEY — DOES IT ACTUALLY WORK? (5 personas simulated against a fresh clone)
refuted_claims.title: `export_skills.py --install` drops 1027 skills into .claude/skills/ (~134K tokens of descriptions) and installs no commands, agents, or CLAUDE.md
refuted_claims.reason:
The mechanical observation reproduces (`--install` does write 1027 skills into `.agents/skills/` + `.claude/skills/` symlinks and nothing else), but the claim is built on a false premise: that `export_skills.py --install` is the Claude Code install path. It is not. The Claude Code path is a first-class, already-shipped **tiered plugin** — `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` + `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, generated by `scripts/build_plugin.py`, documented in `/Users/pranavnagrecha/VS Code/Personal/SfSkills/docs/installing-the-plugin.md`, and verified there against a real Claude Code v2.1.209 `marketplace add` -> `install` -> `details` cycle.

The repo's `.claude/skills/` contains exactly **12 router skills** (salesforce + 11 domain routers), not 1027. `python3 scripts/build_plugin.py --measure` reports Tier-1 always-on cost of **2,723 tokens** vs `flat_export_tokens: 133935` — i.e. the repo independently computes the *same* number the claim presents as a discovery (claim says 134,449; repo says 133,935), labels it "134k tokens of index before the first question", and has a build gate that **exits 1 if Tier 1 crosses 6,000 tokens or 5% of flat-export cost**. So the concern is not merely known, it is engineered against, measured, documented, and CI-gated.

Each sub-assertion of "installs no commands, agents, or CLAUDE.md" is also satisfied elsewhere: the plugin ships **66 slash commands and 48 agents** (`commands: 66, agents: 48` from `--measure`; Tier-3 agents at `.claude/agents/<id>.md`), `scripts/install_local_commands.py` installs the 66 commands standalone, `docs/installing-single-agents.md` covers shipping one agent into another project, and README's Install section says "Claude Code picks the repo up automatically via CLAUDE.md".

Finally the claim omits that `--install` is explicitly a **cross-tool** convenience (`.agents/skills/` is the Codex / Gemini CLI / Cursor>=2.4 convention per its own `--help`) and that it takes `--domain`/`--skill` filters — the script's own docstring example is `--install ~/dev/my-sf-project --domain apex`, not an unfiltered 1027-skill dump. The printed banner lists "Claude Code: skills/ is the canonical source" as a *separate* line from the "One-command" line.

Residual: at most a P3 docs nit — the `One-command` banner line in `scripts/export_skills.py:1124` could cross-reference `docs/installing-the-plugin.md` so a Claude Code user doesn't mistake the cross-tool installer for the Claude path. That is a one-line print statement, not a P1.
refuted_claims.corrected: `export_skills.py --install` is a cross-tool installer (`.agents/skills/` per the Codex/Gemini/Cursor>=2.4 convention, plus `.claude/skills` symlinks) and, run unfiltered, does write all 1027 skills — but it is NOT the Claude Code install path and never claimed to be. Claude Code installs via the shipped tiered plugin (`/plugin marketplace add PranavNagrecha/AwesomeSalesforceSkills` + `/plugin install sfskills@sfskills`), which loads 12 router skills + 66 commands at ~2,723 always-on tokens (2% of a flat export, a ~49x reduction), reaches the 1027 packages on demand and the 48 agents on invocation, and fails the build if Tier 1 exceeds 6,000 tokens. refuted_claims.reason:
Two of the three pillars of this claim are fabricated or contradicted by the repo.

(1) FABRICATED EVIDENCE. The claim quotes "README.md line 429" and "README.md line 316". README.md is 197 lines long. `grep -rn 'assess.org|org-assessor' README.md` returns ZERO hits — README.md never mentions /assess-org, never mentions org-assessor, and never says "Run agents/org-assessor against a live org via the MCP server". Their own pasted evidence output shows a README.md:429 line that their own command cannot have produced (my re-run of their exact command returned only the CLAUDE.md:193 hit). The entire "README oversells /assess-org" half of the finding is invented.

(2) THE CONTRACT EXPLICITLY EXEMPTS class:build. agents/_shared/AGENT_CONTRACT.md:42 states "The required section shape depends on the agent's `class`." Lines 44-56 define the 8-section shape for `class: runtime` ONLY. Lines 57-67 define a separate 5-section shape for `class: build` (What This Agent Does / Invocation / Mandatory Reads / Plan / What This Agent Does NOT Do) and state build agents "MAY include Inputs, Output Contract (alias: Output Format), and Escalation / Refusal Rules when those concepts apply." Line 76 lists `Output Format` as an accepted alias for `Output Contract` — org-assessor HAS `## Output Format`, which the claim counted as missing. org-assessor satisfies all five required build sections plus the optional Output Contract. `python3 scripts/validate_repo.py --agents` validates all 76 agents and reports ZERO structural errors on org-assessor, code-reviewer or release-planner (the only 9 errors are unrelated 47-vs-48 doc-count drift). scripts/migrate_deliverable_contract.py:40-42 documents the DELIVERABLE_CONTRACT exemption in-repo: "code-reviewer (class=build) ... don't need this flag."

(3) ABSENCE FROM THE RUNTIME ROSTER IS BY DESIGN, NOT DRIFT. agents/_shared/RUNTIME_VS_BUILD.md lines 3-24 list all three under "## Build-time agents", with org-assessor annotated "Audits a target org against the library (operator tool)". They are excluded from the runtime roster in CLAUDE.md deliberately because they are not runtime agents.

(4) NO "LIVE ORG" OVERSELL EXISTS. commands/assess-org.md:11 says "Point the agent at an SFDX project directory or metadata export" — exactly consistent with `requires_org: false`. There is no contradicting doc anywhere; the contradiction was manufactured from the fabricated README line.

Surviving kernel (minor, ~P3): org-assessor and waf-assessor (class: runtime) do overlap on WAF scoring, and neither AGENT.md nor either command file cross-references the other (`grep -rn 'assess-waf|waf-assessor' commands/assess-org.md agents/org-assessor/AGENT.md` → no hits; org-assessor's Related Agents lists only code-reviewer and release-planner). That is a one-line disambiguation nit, not a P1 broken entry point.
refuted_claims.corrected: org-assessor / code-reviewer / release-planner are `class: build` BY DESIGN (RUNTIME_VS_BUILD.md lists all three as build-time agents; org-assessor is labelled an "operator tool"), and AGENT_CONTRACT.md:42,57-67 explicitly defines a separate, shorter 5-section shape for class:build agents in which Inputs / Output Contract / Escalation Rules are optional and `Output Format` is an accepted alias for `Output Contract`. All three pass `validate_repo.py --agents` with zero structural errors. README.md contains no mention of /assess-org or org-assessor at all (file is 197 lines; the cited lines 316 and 429 do not exist), so there is no "live org via MCP" oversell and no contradiction with commands/assess-org.md or `requires_org: false`. The only real residue is cosmetic: /assess-org (build, WAF-scored org report) and /assess-waf (waf-assessor, runtime) overlap in scope with no cross-reference in either direction — worth one "see also" line each, severity P3.

refuted_claims.title: 158 of 1027 skills satisfy the mandatory Recommended Workflow section with identical filler that gives the AI no domain-specific procedure
refuted_claims.reason:
The raw counts reproduce (158 SKILL.md files match the filler line; 1027 skill dirs), so the surface observation is real. But three load-bearing parts of the claim are wrong or overstated.

(1) "158 skills ... identical filler" — only 149 workflow blocks are byte-identical (md5 2fa74f99...); the remaining ~11 are domain-varied edits of the same spine, and one has 13 steps. So the byte-identical population is 149/1027 = 14.5%, not 158.

(2) "gives the AI no domain-specific procedure" is false for the flagship example the claim picks. In skills/admin/assignment-rules/SKILL.md the workflow is a 5-step *spine that routes into* domain-specific content in the same file: step 3 points at Core Concepts + Common Patterns (lines 58-171, assignment-rule specific), step 4 points at the Review Checklist immediately below (lines 198-213: "only one assignment rule is active per object", "catch-all entry is last", "Sforce-Auto-Assign: true header (REST) or AssignmentRuleHeader (SOAP)", "Data Loader imports have sfdc.assignmentRule set", "round-robin Apex: test for concurrency and mixed-DML"). An agent activating this skill reads the whole SKILL.md, not the workflow section in isolation.

(3) "run the skill's checker script" is not a dangling reference. I checked every one of the 160 boilerplate-workflow skills: 0 lack a populated scripts/ directory. assignment-rules ships skills/admin/assignment-rules/scripts/check_assignment_rules.py.

Additionally, 869 of 1027 skills (85%) have bespoke workflows, and 25 of a 40-file sample of the boilerplate set carry a domain-specific "## Review Checklist" the workflow explicitly delegates to. This is a template-consistency/polish issue in ~15% of packages where a generic spine wasn't specialized — legitimate cleanup, but not a P1 "the AI gets no procedure" failure, and not a blocker for Persona 1, who lands on a file whose Before Starting, Core Concepts, Common Patterns, Review Checklist, and Gotchas are all assignment-rule specific.
refuted_claims.corrected: 149 of 1027 skills (14.5%) reuse a byte-identical 5-step "Recommended Workflow" spine (another ~9 use lightly-edited variants), instead of specializing it to the domain. This is a template-specialization debt item, not a content gap: in every one of the 160 affected packages the workflow's step 4 resolves to a real skill-local checker script, and the majority pair it with a domain-specific Review Checklist in the same file (25/40 sampled). The remaining 85% of skills have bespoke workflows. Severity is P3 (consistency/polish), not P1 — the fix is to specialize steps 1, 3, and 5 per domain, ideally by adding a validator gate that rejects the scaffolded default text once a skill leaves draft.

refuted_claims.title: "Output quality is testable, not vibes-based" rests on 10 of 1027 skills across 4 of 11 domains, and the runner only lints file shape
refuted_claims.reason:
The counting facts reproduce exactly (10 golden files: apex 4, integration 3, lwc 2, flow 1; 30 P0 cases; no CI workflow invokes run_evals.py). But the claim's load-bearing conclusion — "no eval in this repo has an automated pass/fail today" — is false, and the "only lints file shape" framing is false, on three independent counts.

(1) A SECOND, DETERMINISTIC eval layer exists that the claim never looked for: `evals/agents/` — 53 fixtures across ~30 runtime agents with `expect:` blocks, 15 committed baselines, and `evals/agents/scripts/run_agent_evals.py`, whose own docstring says "Exit codes: 0 all pass / 1 structural lint failure / 2 P0 rubric failure" and "performs NO network / model calls". `evals/agents/framework.md:76` explicitly tables the two layers as "Grade via | LLM rubric grader | deterministic envelope match". `--grade --envelope <json>` is a fully automated pass/fail with no grader model required. `scripts/execute_agent_fixture.py` is the harness that produces those envelopes (its docstring: "fixture YAML --> this harness --> envelope JSON --> run_agent_evals.py --grade").

(2) `--grader-cmd` is not aspirational — I ran it with a stub grader and got a real gate verdict `[PASS] All P0 gates met.` The runner does score and gate; what is missing is a bundled LLM grader binary, not the scoring machinery.

(3) The grader contract IS documented, contrary to "no default grader is shipped or documented": `evals/README.md` says "The grader contract is defined in `framework.md`", and `evals/framework.md:88,125,136` specifies the 0-5 rubric and the citation requirement.

Finally, the CI gap the claim presents as a discovery is already self-disclosed in three shipped docs: `docs/architecture.md:213-215` ("no workflow invokes `evals/scripts/run_evals.py`, so the golden cases gate nothing"), `docs/comparison.md:110-111` (which even prints the grep), and `docs/positioning.md:156`. This is a documented, tracked limitation, not a hidden overclaim — and `docs/architecture.md` grades the golden layer "Manual only" in the same table where structural validation is "Pre-commit hook and CI", so "Output quality is testable, not vibes-based" is not being sold as automated.
refuted_claims.corrected: Golden output-quality evals cover 10 of 1,027 skills in 4 of 11 domains (apex 4, integration 3, lwc 2, flow 1; 30 P0 cases), leaving admin/architect/data/devops/agentforce/security/omnistudio with no golden eval. `run_evals.py --structure` is a shape lint; real scoring works but requires the caller to supply `--grader-cmd` (verified: a stub grader yields `[PASS] All P0 gates met.`), and no LLM grader is bundled — though the grader rubric contract is documented in `evals/framework.md`. No CI workflow invokes `run_evals.py`, so golden cases gate nothing on merge — a limitation the repo already discloses verbatim in `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/comparison.md`, and `docs/positioning.md`. The claim's conclusion that "no eval in this repo has an automated pass/fail today" is wrong: `evals/agents/` ships 53 fixtures + 15 baselines graded by `run_agent_evals.py --grade` via deterministic envelope match with zero model calls. The accurate residual gap is narrower: (a) golden-eval domain coverage, and (b) neither eval layer is wired into `.github/workflows/`.

refuted_claims.title: 178 MB clone for 33.5 MB of content — 518 dead versions of vector_index/chunks.jsonl are still in main's history
refuted_claims.reason:
The underlying physical fact (dead vector_index blobs sit in the pack) is real, but every load-bearing part of the claim is wrong: the numbers, the "nobody noticed" framing, and the quoted BACKLOG text.

1) ALREADY DOCUMENTED AS A DELIBERATE DEFERRAL, dated today. `/Users/pranavnagrecha/VS Code/Personal/SfSkills/.gitignore` lines 16-31 carry a measured 2026-07-31 analysis: ".git is 524 MB ... vector_index/chunks.jsonl, 206 committed revisions totalling 11,651 MB uncompressed, last tracked at 59e265ce6 ... The rules above stop future growth. They cannot shrink an existing clone ... Only a history rewrite (git filter-repo, git lfs migrate) would reclaim them, and that is deliberately out of scope." `/Users/pranavnagrecha/VS Code/Personal/SfSkills/BACKLOG.md` lines 22-42 carry the same finding under "Clone weight (originally: Git LFS for lexical.sqlite)" with **Status (2026-07-31)**, **Why deferred**, and **Work needed**. `docs/installing-the-plugin.md:282` ("### 4. The clone is heavy") and `docs/comparison.md:86` also state it to users. This is a documented, dated, reasoned decision — not an unnoticed gap.

2) THE BACKLOG QUOTE IS STALE/FABRICATED. The claim quotes the trigger as "When the repo clone size starts causing CI slowdowns, or when a contributor reports the repo is slow to clone" and asserts "the trigger has already fired". That string does not exist anywhere in the repo. The actual current trigger (BACKLOG.md:38) is "A contributor reports the clone is unworkable, or registry/skills.json ... starts dominating growth the way chunks.jsonl did." No contributor report exists, and registry/skills.json (766 MB / 221 revisions) is still smaller than chunks.jsonl's historical 11,651 MB. The trigger has NOT fired.

3) THE HEADLINE NUMBERS ARE WRONG. "33.5 MB of content" is a measurement bug: `git ls-files -z | xargs -0 du -ck | tail -1` splits into two xargs batches and `tail -1` keeps only the second total (68000 + 34140 KB). Correct tracked tree = 80.7 MB across 9,229 files — the number the repo's own docs already publish. The bare clone measures 193 MB here, not 178 MB.

4) "518 dead versions of vector_index/chunks.jsonl" conflates paths. Broken down by path on origin/main: chunks.jsonl 90.6 MB / 103 versions; lexical.sqlite 46.0 MB / 30 versions; query-fixtures.json 0.6 MB / 160 versions; manifest.json ~0 MB / 224 versions. The latter two are STILL TRACKED (`git ls-files vector_index/`), so 384 of the 518 "dead" versions are live-path history, and chunks.jsonl accounts for 103 versions, not 518.

Severity P0 is not supportable: nothing is broken, the condition is documented in three places, the remedy is explicitly rejected as SHA-invalidating, and no re-clone is required for any workflow.
refuted_claims.corrected: A bare clone of main is 193 MB against an 80.7 MB tracked tree; ~137 MB of pack is historical vector_index blobs, of which vector_index/chunks.jsonl (90.6 MB across 103 revisions, last tracked at 59e265ce6) and lexical.sqlite (46.0 MB / 30 revisions) are now-gitignored dead weight. This is already measured and documented as a deliberate deferral in .gitignore:16-31 and BACKLOG.md:22-42 ("Clone weight"), with history rewrite rejected because it invalidates every existing clone, fork, and the commit SHAs cited in docs. The documented trigger — a contributor reporting the clone unworkable, or registry/skills.json dominating growth — has not fired. Severity is at most P3/informational, not P0.

refuted_claims.title: 142 dated session artifacts are committed to main, violating the repo's own stated 'no session artifacts' rule
refuted_claims.reason:
The file counts reproduce exactly, but the framing is wrong. 122 of the 142 files (86%) are in `docs/validation/`, which the repo does NOT treat as session waste — it treats it as a deliberately committed audit trail, and says so in three independent places:

1. `docs/validation/README.md` per-file table for Layer 4 marks `*.raw.md`, `*.envelope.json`, `*.grade.txt` as "(committed)" and `*.prompt.txt` as "reproducible, gitignored", and the "When to re-run" section states: "Each writes a dated report to `docs/validation/`. **Commit the reports with the change that prompted them — the reports become part of the audit trail.**"

2. The very `.gitignore` the claim cites as the counter-authority already contains a targeted rule for this directory and explicitly carves the rest IN:
```
docs/validation/agent_executions_*/*.prompt.txt
# ... The raw.md (model response), envelope.json (extracted
# envelope), and grade.txt (grader verdict) alongside it ARE committed as the
# persistent record of each agent execution.
```
So the assertion that the session-artifact rule "was never applied to `docs/validation/`" is false — it was applied, deliberately, at file-type granularity.

3. These files are load-bearing links in shipped docs, not orphans: `README.md:109`, `docs/positioning.md:97-99` (deep-links `probe_report_2026-04-17.md`, `agent_smoke_rollup_2026-04-19.md`, `skill_factuality_2026-04-17.md` as the evidence table), `docs/comparison.md:114`, and `.github/workflows/org-validation.yml`. Deleting them would break published documentation.

The same applies to `.planning/`: the "no session artifacts" rule WAS applied there — `.gitignore` carries four `.planning`-specific rules (`scaffolds-pending/`, `build-history/`, `qa-execution/`, `qa-*.md`), and `commands/build-skills.md:26` cites the rule by name. Of the 20 tracked `.planning` files, `mcp-v0.2-plan.md` is linked from `CHANGELOG.md:227` as the plan-of-record and `skill-backlog.md` is a live backlog referenced by `feedback/README.md:56` — neither is a dated session dump.

What survives is far smaller: ~18 files (17 `skill-gap-verification-2026-05-*.md` dailies plus `system-inventory-2026-05-01.md`), totalling ~230 KB, with zero inbound references anywhere in the repo (`grep -rn "gap-verification" AGENT_RULES.md CLAUDE.md commands/ docs/ agents/` returns nothing). That is real hygiene debt but it is ~13% of the claimed file count, ~1.4% of the 9,229 tracked files, and cosmetic next to the byte problem the `.gitignore` header already documents at length (`registry/skills.json`, 766 MB across 221 revisions, tracked by design). P3, not P1.
refuted_claims.corrected: 17 dated `skill-gap-verification-YYYY-MM-DD.md` dailies (May 2026) plus `system-inventory-2026-05-01.md` are tracked under `.planning/` with no inbound reference from any doc, command, script, or workflow — ~18 files / ~230 KB of undocumented session output. Unlike the sibling `.planning/build-history/`, `.planning/scaffolds-pending/`, `.planning/qa-execution/`, and `.planning/qa-*.md` (all explicitly gitignored), and unlike `.planning/mcp-v0.2-plan.md` (linked from CHANGELOG.md:227) and `.planning/skill-backlog.md`, these dailies were never given a gitignore rule or a documented retention rationale. The `docs/validation/` tree (122 files) is NOT part of this gap: it is an intentionally committed audit trail, documented as such in `docs/validation/README.md`, given a deliberate file-type-level gitignore rule (`docs/validation/agent_executions_*/*.prompt.txt` only), and deep-linked from README.md, docs/positioning.md, docs/comparison.md, and .github/workflows/org-validation.yml. (b) The 567 MB of dotdirs is ALREADY SATISFIED: `git check-ignore -v` confirms .build-venv, .qa-venv, .smoke-venv, .verify-venv, .intake-reports, and .claude/worktrees are all ignored, and .gitignore carries multi-line comments explaining the venv and intake-report policy specifically. Local disk usage on the author's machine is not a repo-structure defect. (c) 2 of 3 'near-dead' dirs are load-bearing: batches/TEMPLATE.yaml is the input contract for two shipped scripts (its old mtime is expected for a stable template — real batch files are user-supplied and untracked), and feedback/FEEDBACK_LOG.md is anchor-linked from the agents/_shared contract layer, so deleting it breaks provenance references. (d) `.claude/worktrees` is described as 'an orphaned agent worktree from 2026-04-28' (singular) but `git worktree list` shows 11, 10 of them prunable harness state. Residual real finding: `_codex_drops/` only.
refuted_claims.corrected: Exactly one top-level directory is genuinely dead: `_codex_drops/` (2 tracked files, last commit 2026-04-16, referenced nowhere except itself and .gitignore). `batches/` and `feedback/` are NOT abandoned — `batches/TEMPLATE.yaml` is the documented input contract for `scripts/ship_skills.py` and `scripts/skill_forge.py` (both invoke `--batch batches/*.yaml`), and `feedback/FEEDBACK_LOG.md` is cited by stable anchor from at least 5 live docs including `agents/_shared/CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md`, `agents/_shared/AGENT_DISAMBIGUATION.md`, `agents/_shared/probes/automation-graph-for-sobject.md`, and `docs/agent-invocation-modes.md`. refuted_claims.title: 6 stale local branches, 10 prunable worktree registrations, 1 orphaned 345 MB worktree, and 8 abandoned stashes
refuted_claims.reason:
The raw numbers reproduce exactly (10 prunable worktrees at 6e05447ce, 1 detached-HEAD worktree at 345 MB, 8 `WIP on main` stashes from 2026-04-06..04-13, 6 non-main local branches with the stated ahead/behind counts). But the claim is overstated as a P1 "repo structure and hygiene" defect on three independent counts.

(1) NOT REPO CONTENT. `.claude/worktrees` is gitignored — `git check-ignore -v` resolves it to `.gitignore:81: .claude/*`. Worktree registrations live in `.git/worktrees`, stashes in `.git/refs/stash`, local branches in `.git/refs/heads`. None of it is tracked, none of it ships in a clone, none of it is visible to any other contributor, none of it is touched by `scripts/validate_repo.py`, `skill_sync.py`, or CI. This is one developer's laptop state, not a property of the repository. A hygiene lens over `skills/`, `registry/`, `vector_index/`, `docs/` finds nothing here.

(2) THE "10 PRUNABLE REGISTRATIONS" ARE 4.4 MB OF METADATA, NOT DISK BLOAT. Their working directories do not exist on disk at all — `ls -d .claude/worktrees/agent-*` returns "no matches found"; `du -sh .claude/worktrees` shows 345 M total, all of it the single `goofy-northcutt-9e40aa` dir. "Prunable" is precisely git telling you the admin record outlived the directory. `du -sh .git/worktrees` = 4.4 M across all 11 entries. One `git worktree prune` clears it; there is no 10× storage problem to describe.

(3) THE BRANCH LIST IS MISCHARACTERIZED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Three of the six are backed on origin — `onboard-tdd-sf-2026-07-08` and `upstream-learnings-2026-07-06` are byte-identical to their remotes (a76c1469…/a76c1469…, c606b084…/c606b084…), so calling them "stale local branches" is wrong: they are local mirrors of remote refs and deleting them loses nothing because nothing was ever only there. Conversely, `claude/goofy-northcutt-9e40aa` (406 unique commits) and `claude/hopeful-tereshkova` (276 unique) do NOT exist on origin at all — `git ls-remote --heads origin | grep -E "goofy|hopeful|reconcile"` exits 1 with no output. Those two are the opposite of cruft: they are the only copies of 682 commits. Recommending their deletion under a "stale branch cleanup" P1 is a data-loss recommendation, not a hygiene fix.

Net: real observation, wrong severity and wrong remedy. Correct handling is `git worktree prune` (safe, instant), then a deliberate keep/discard decision on the two remote-less branches, with the stashes and the 345 MB worktree as optional reclaim.
refuted_claims.corrected: P3 (local workspace hygiene, not a repo defect): the developer's working copy carries 11 stale entries in `.git/worktrees` — 10 registrations whose directories no longer exist (4.4 MB of metadata, cleared by `git worktree prune`) plus one live detached-HEAD worktree at `.claude/worktrees/goofy-northcutt-9e40aa` occupying 345 MB — along with 8 April-2026 `WIP on main` stashes. All of it is gitignored (`.gitignore:81: .claude/*`) or lives inside `.git/`, so it is invisible to clones, contributors, CI, and `validate_repo.py`; no tracked file is affected. Of the six non-main local branches, `onboard-tdd-sf-2026-07-08` and `upstream-learnings-2026-07-06` are byte-identical to their origin counterparts and safe to delete, while `claude/goofy-northcutt-9e40aa` (406 commits) and `claude/hopeful-tereshkova` (276 commits) exist on no remote and must NOT be blanket-deleted as "stale" — they are the sole copies of that work.

refuted_claims.title: docs/ has no README or index and mixes generated catalogs, user docs, internal analysis dumps, and a dead proposal in one flat namespace
refuted_claims.reason:
Two of the claim's load-bearing facts are wrong against the current repo.

(1) "No README or index" is false. `docs/README.md` exists (7,761 bytes) and is precisely the artifact the gap asks for: a 6-section index of EVERY doc in the repo, with an explicit `Consumer` / `Contributor` / `Both` audience legend, and with exactly the content-class separation the claim says is missing — Section 5 "Reference and generated artifacts" prefixed "Never hand-edit anything in this section" (SKILLS.md, queue-progress.md, reports/duplicate-candidates.md), and Section 6 "Historical" which explicitly disposes of the allegedly-dead proposal: "QUEUE_FORMAT_PROPOSAL.md ... Superseded — BACKLOG.yaml and queue-progress.md now exist exactly as proposed." It also pre-empts the "internal analysis dump" complaint by labelling agent-informal-invocation-analysis.md "1,169 lines — reference, not reading", and closes with a "Documents this index does not cover" note explaining docs/reports/ holds runtime working artifacts. Caveat and the only residual work: docs/README.md and 10 sibling docs (architecture.md, faq.md, getting-started.md, glossary.md, troubleshooting.md, positioning.md, comparison.md, go-to-market.md, installing-the-plugin.md, worked-example-trigger-consolidation.md) are UNTRACKED (`?? docs/README.md`), so a fresh clone at HEAD does not yet get them. That is a "commit these" chore, not a P1 information-architecture gap.

(2) The docs/reports/ "path that does not exist in a fresh clone" framing is wrong. CLAUDE.md's mandatory step 2 is two bullets: the first bullet RUNS `python3 scripts/audit_duplicates.py --domain <domain>`, which is the script that writes the file — `scripts/audit_duplicates.py:45` is `REPORT_PATH = ROOT / "docs" / "reports" / "duplicate-candidates.md"` and its module docstring at line 16 says "The report is written to ``docs/reports/duplicate-candidates.md`` (overwritten)." The second bullet then says review it. Gitignoring a deterministically regenerated, overwritten-per-run report is correct hygiene, not a broken reference.

(3) The file inventory is stale: docs/ top level now holds 20 markdown files, not 9.
refuted_claims.corrected: docs/README.md — a complete, audience-labelled index that classifies generated vs consumer vs contributor vs historical docs and explicitly marks QUEUE_FORMAT_PROPOSAL.md as superseded — already exists in the working tree, along with 10 other new user-facing docs (getting-started, architecture, faq, glossary, troubleshooting, positioning, comparison, go-to-market, installing-the-plugin, worked-example-trigger-consolidation). The only real residual is P3 and mechanical: all 11 are untracked and need to be committed so a fresh clone gets them. The docs/reports/ portion of the claim is simply incorrect — that path is generated on demand by scripts/audit_duplicates.py, which CLAUDE.md instructs contributors to run in the bullet immediately preceding the "review the report" bullet.

p2_gaps.title: install_local_commands.py performs a 65-file write when passed --help, and the README's operator table links to a command file that does not exist
p2_gaps.what_is_missing: scripts/install_local_commands.py has no argparse — `main()` runs unconditionally, so `python3 scripts/install_local_commands.py --help` silently copied 65 files into .claude/commands/ (added=2 updated=63) instead of printing usage. I hit this by accident while auditing. Separately, README.md's 'Operators drive the system via slash commands' table links `[/run-queue](./commands/run-queue.md)` as its first row; that file does not exist (1 broken link out of 71 checked). The MCP package also declares `license = { text = "MIT" }` in mcp/sfskills-mcp/pyproject.toml while the repo LICENSE is Apache-2.0.

p2_gaps.why_it_matters: A script that writes 65 files when the user asks it what it does is a trust violation on a repo whose entire pitch is deterministic, safe tooling — and `install_local_commands.py` is the very script new users must run (per the gitignore finding above), so `--help` is a likely first interaction. The dead /run-queue link is the first row of the operator table, so the first thing an evaluating maintainer clicks 404s. The license mismatch will matter the moment anyone vendors the MCP package.
p2_gaps.proposed_fix: Add argparse to scripts/install_local_commands.py with `--dry-run` (print the plan) and make it the behaviour for `--help`/unknown flags; audit the other stdlib scripts in scripts/ for the same no-argparse pattern. Either restore commands/run-queue.md or repoint that README row at commands/build-skills.md (the surviving batch builder). Set mcp/sfskills-mcp/pyproject.toml license to Apache-2.0 to match LICENSE, and add the README link check to the existing pr-lint workflow so broken links fail CI.

p2_gaps.what_is_missing: `scripts/` has 44 top-level .py files with no grouping. Five of them are one-time schema migrations that will never be run again — `backfill_agent_frontmatter.py`, `backfill_inputs_schema_descriptions.py`, `migrate_agent_dependencies.py`, `migrate_deliverable_contract.py`, `migrate_multidim_dimensions.py` — sitting alphabetically interleaved with the five scripts CLAUDE.md declares 'Required' (`skill_sync.py`, `validate_repo.py`, `search_knowledge.py`). A `scripts/_migrations/` subdirectory already exists and holds 3 such scripts, so the convention was established and then not followed.

p2_gaps.why_it_matters: An AI agent or contributor told to 'sync the repo' does `ls scripts/` and sees 44 equally-weighted options with no signal about which 5 are the daily drivers. Then group the remainder into `scripts/build/` (build_index, build_registry, build_knowledge, build_skill_embeddings, generate_docs, generate_queue_dashboard, generate_validation_index, export_skills, export_agent_bundle), `scripts/validate/` (validate_repo, validate_skill_factuality, validate_probes_against_org, check_doc_counts, run_all_checkers, audit_duplicates, smoke_test_agents), and `scripts/author/` (new_skill, new_agent, onboard_source, skill_forge, run_builder, queue_reader), leaving only `skill_sync.py` and `search_knowledge.py` at scripts/ root as the two commands anyone actually types. Update CLAUDE.md, AGENT_RULES.md, and the 65 commands/*.md paths in one pass.

p2_gaps.title: Only 2 of 65 command slugs match their agent directory name, and 14 deprecated agents are visually indistinguishable in a flat agents/ listing
p2_gaps.what_is_missing: `commands/*.md` and `agents/*/` use two independent naming schemes: commands are verb-first (`refactor-apex`, `build-lwc`, `design-object`), agents are noun-first (`apex-refactorer`, `lwc-builder`, `object-designer`). Only 2 of 65 command names have a same-named agent directory. Separately, `ls agents/` returns 76 flat entries in which the 14 `status: deprecated` legacy aliases (`sharing-audit-agent`, `record-type-and-layout-auditor`, `picklist-governor`, …) are indistinguishable from the 47 active runtime agents and 14 build-time agents — the class and status live in frontmatter, so you must open each file to tell.

p2_gaps.why_it_matters: Mitigated, not eliminated: every command file does link its agent by explicit relative path, so an agent following the docs resolves correctly. But a human debugging `/audit-sharing` cannot guess it lives in `agents/sharing-audit-agent/`, and cannot see from a directory listing that it is one of 14 deprecated aliases that should redirect to `/audit-router`. This is the kind of friction that makes contributors give up on their first PR.
p2_gaps.proposed_fix: Do not rename 65+75 things — the churn is not worth it. Instead: (1) add an `agent:` field to each `commands/*.md` frontmatter and a `command:` field to each `agents/*/AGENT.md` frontmatter, then have `validate_repo.py` assert the pair resolves both ways (this makes the mapping machine-checkable rather than prose-only); (2) move the 14 `status: deprecated` agents into `agents/_deprecated/` and the 14 `class: build` agents into `agents/_build/`, leaving `ls agents/` showing exactly the 47 active runtime agents — matching what README and CLAUDE.md advertise. Update SKILL_MAP.md and RUNTIME_VS_BUILD.md paths in the same commit.
